title: [React InstantSearch Core]: `useInstantsearch` hook will return 0 hits on init with an idle state, before loading

comments.body:
I think the logic to choose idle as the initial state is that the InstantSearch instance isn't yet started, so technically the first search isn't yet fired. You can use `results.__isArtificial` to work around this for now (will be `true` in the initial pre-load state).

What do you change in the PR that addresses this? Happy to have a look and discuss to see what behaviour is more correct / less surprising.

Thanks for the quick reply! The PR would do exactly that, check the `results.__isArtificial` property to check if the results aren't artificial. I had another implementation in mind, where there's another `hasReceivedResults` prop on the `SearchResultsApi` interface. You can see how it would be implemented [here](https://github.com/tharropoulos/instantsearch/commit/09508a10841663445789d1a5249ef1cefca5b89d).

The only thing I'm not stoked about currently, is that it feels a bit scary using internal variables inside client code, since there's no guarantee that the behavior will remain consistent as time goes on.

Also, just because I was checking the library out, there's a small change that could be beneficial for DX in regards to the dunder prefix (`__`) using tilde (`~`) prefix instead, since that will de-prioritize the property in autocomplete. Credits to [colinhacks](https://x.com/colinhacks/status/1816860780459073933).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d27a522-9d83-4a3d-bf68-67a5c869b6a2)

It has two underscores to ensure it isn't overridden by any property from the search API in the future and that we don't override a real property (one underscore is reserved for the engine-internal response attributes, two therefore for InstantSearch).

You can safely use this property, it's not internal.

I didn't know about the ~ for internal properties, could be useful in the future, but changing now would be breaking. automaticInsights for example comes from the search engine response directly

Sure, I'll use it in the client app then. If you decide on either adding an `init` state or look into defaulting to what I suggested with the `hasReceivedResults` or the `__ArtificialResults` check, I'll be happy to open a PR for it.

Closing this issue then 🔍

Sounds good. I think if we want to change the default status, it's more a question of changing https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/master/packages/instantsearch.js/src/lib/InstantSearch.ts#L246 to `loading`, but that feels a bit odd in InstantSearch.js, maybe only for React InstantSearch
Sure, up to you. Just tag me and I'll take a look. Thanks for open-sourcing the library! Excellent work
